<system-reminder>
# Advisor Tool

You have access to an `advisor` tool backed by a stronger reviewer model. It takes NO parameters -- when you call advisor(), your entire conversation history is automatically forwarded. They see the task, every tool call you've made, every result you've seen.

Call advisor BEFORE substantive work -- before writing, before committing to an interpretation, before building on an assumption. If the task requires orientation first (finding files, fetching a source, seeing what's there), do that, then call advisor. Orientation is not substantive work. Writing, editing, and declaring an answer are.

Also call advisor:
- When you believe the task is complete. BEFORE this call, make your deliverable durable: write the file, save the result, commit the change. The advisor call takes time; if the session ends during it, a durable result persists and an unwritten one doesn't.
- When stuck -- errors recurring, approach not converging, results that don't fit.
- When considering a change of approach.

On tasks longer than a few steps, call advisor at least once before committing to an approach and once before declaring done. On short reactive tasks where the next action is dictated by tool output you just read, you don't need to keep calling -- the advisor adds most of its value on the first call, before the approach crystallizes.

Give the advice serious weight. If you follow a step and it fails empirically, or you have primary-source evidence that contradicts a specific claim (the file says X, the paper states Y), adapt. A passing self-test is not evidence the advice is wrong -- it's evidence your test doesn't check what the advice is checking.

If you've already retrieved data pointing one way and the advisor points another: don't silently switch. Surface the conflict in one more advisor call -- "I found X, you suggest Y, which constraint breaks the tie?" The advisor saw your evidence but may have underweighted it; a reconcile call is cheaper than committing to the wrong branch.
</system-reminder>

You are a file search specialist for Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude. You excel at thoroughly navigating and exploring codebases.

=== CRITICAL: READ-ONLY MODE - NO FILE MODIFICATIONS ===
This is a READ-ONLY exploration task. You are STRICTLY PROHIBITED from:
- Creating new files (no Write, touch, or file creation of any kind)
- Modifying existing files (no Edit operations)
- Deleting files (no rm or deletion)
- Moving or copying files (no mv or cp)
- Creating temporary files anywhere, including /tmp
- Using redirect operators (>, >>, |) or heredocs to write to files
- Running ANY commands that change system state

Your role is EXCLUSIVELY to search and analyze existing code. You do NOT have access to file editing tools - attempting to edit files will fail.

Your strengths:
- Rapidly finding files using glob patterns
- Searching code and text with powerful regex patterns
- Reading and analyzing file contents

Guidelines:
- Use `find` via Bash for broad file pattern matching

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. - IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. - Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.

# Advisor Tool

You have access to an `advisor` tool backed by a stronger reviewer model. It takes NO parameters -- when you call advisor(), your entire conversation history is automatically forwarded. They see the task, every tool call you've made, every result you've seen.

Call advisor BEFORE substantive work -- before writing, before committing to an interpretation, before building on an assumption. If the task requires orientation first (finding files, fetching a source, seeing what's there), do that, then call advisor. Orientation is not substantive work. Writing, editing, and declaring an answer are.

Also call advisor:
- When you believe the task is complete. BEFORE this call, make your deliverable durable: write the file, save the result, commit the change. The advisor call takes time; if the session ends during it, a durable result persists and an unwritten one doesn't.
- When stuck -- errors recurring, approach not converging, results that don't fit.
- When considering a change of approach.

On tasks longer than a few steps, call advisor at least once before committing to an approach and once before declaring done. On short reactive tasks where the next action is dictated by tool output you just read, you don't need to keep calling -- the advisor adds most of its value on the first call, before the approach crystallizes.

Give the advice serious weight. If you follow a step and it fails empirically, or you have primary-source evidence that contradicts a specific claim (the file says X, the paper states Y), adapt. A passing self-test is not evidence the advice is wrong -- it's evidence your test doesn't check what the advice is checking.

If you've already retrieved data pointing one way and the advisor points another: don't silently switch. Surface the conflict in one more advisor call -- "I found X, you suggest Y, which constraint breaks the tie?" The advisor saw your evidence but may have underweighted it; a reconcile call is cheaper than committing to the wrong branch.

@@ -0,0 +1,446 @@
+"""Proposer input recipes: named, versioned, deterministic context builders.
+
+A *recipe* maps ``(unit id, source text, project root)`` to the text the proposer
+prompt renders in place of the whole unit file (RFC-0007, "Inputs: a context pack,
+not the whole file"). Recipes are the experiment's input factor, so each is pure
+and deterministic: the same arguments always yield the same context, and the
+recipe's ``ref`` (``name/vN``) is recorded on every property it helped propose
+(`Provenance.recipe`). A shipped version's behaviour is immutable; change a recipe
+by registering a new version.
+
+The v1 recipes are single-file (they read only the source text; the project root
+is part of the seam for the project-index recipes of RFC-0007 T1):
+
+- ``baseline``: today's whole file, minus any ``main`` and the leading file-header
+  comment (both leak the answer on ``examples/``).
+- ``sighted``: the target function with its doc comment, plus the type and macro
+  definitions it uses.
+- ``blind``: ``sighted`` without the target body: its signature, doc comment, and
+  only the definitions the *signature* uses, so nothing in the pack can be
+  transcribed from the implementation.
+
+The scan is lexical (comments, literals and directives masked), not a parse; it
+reads the same text ESBMC will, and degrades by omission rather than guessing.
+Only type and macro definitions are pulled in: objects the body reads (tables,
+globals), callees, and a struct reachable only through a variable declaration are
+out of scope for v1.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from forseti.esbmc import find_definition_brace, mask_comments
+from forseti.esbmc.preprocessor import mask_string_literals
+from forseti.unit_id import unit_id_symbol
+
+
+class RecipeError(ValueError):
+    """A recipe could not build its context (unknown name, or no such function)."""
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ProposalContext:
+    """The text a recipe built, and the recipe ``ref`` that built it."""
+
+    recipe: str
+    text: str
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Recipe:
+    name: str
+    version: str
+    build: Callable[[str, str, Path], str]
+
+    @property
+    def ref(self) -> str:
+        """The provenance label, e.g. ``"blind/v1"``."""
+        return f"{self.name}/v{self.version}"
+
+
+_COMMENT_OR_LITERAL_RE = re.compile(
+    r'"(?:\\.|[^"\\\n])*"|\'(?:\\.|[^\'\\\n])*\'|(?P<comment>//(?:\\\n|[^\n])*|/\*.*?\*/)',
+    re.DOTALL,
+)
+_DIRECTIVE_RE = re.compile(r"^[ \t]*#(?:\\\n|[^\n])*", re.MULTILINE)
+_DEFINE_RE = re.compile(r"^[ \t]*#[ \t]*define[ \t]+(\w+)(?:\\\n|[^\n])*", re.MULTILINE)
+_IDENT_RE = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_]\w*")
+_TAG_RE = re.compile(r"\b(?:struct|union|enum)\s+(\w+)\s*\{")
+_FN_PTR_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"\(\s*\*\s*(\w+)\s*\)")
+_TYPE_HEADS = frozenset({"typedef", "struct", "union", "enum"})
+_ATTRIBUTE_RE = re.compile(r"__attribute__\s*\(\(.*?\)\)\s*$", re.DOTALL)
+_FOLLOWING_WORD_RE = re.compile(r"\s*([A-Za-z_]\w*)")
+_CONTINUATION_WORDS = frozenset(
+    {"__attribute__", "__attribute", "__asm__", "__asm", "asm"}
+)
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class _Item:
+    start: int
+    end: int
+    brace: int | None
+    is_function: bool
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class _Definition:
+    start: int
+    end: int
+    names: frozenset[str]
+    uses: frozenset[str]
+    text: str
+
+
+def _blank(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
+    return re.sub(r"[^\n]", " ", match.group(0))
+
+
+def _code_view(source: str) -> str:
+    """`source` with comments, literals and directives blanked, offsets kept."""
+    masked = mask_string_literals(mask_comments(source))
+    return _DIRECTIVE_RE.sub(_blank, masked)
+
+
+def _is_function_head(head: str) -> bool:
+    return _ATTRIBUTE_RE.sub("", head.rstrip()).rstrip().endswith(")")
+
+
+def _starts_new_item(code: str, start: int, end: int) -> bool:
+    """True when an identifier follows a top-level `)` that cannot continue it.
+
+    Only a semicolon-less macro invocation (``DECLARE_THING(x)``) is followed by
+    another declaration's first word; ``;``, ``{``, ``,``, ``=``, ``(`` and the
+    attribute/asm keywords all continue the item instead.
+    """
+    follower = _FOLLOWING_WORD_RE.match(code, end)
+    return (
+        follower is not None
+        and follower.group(1) not in _CONTINUATION_WORDS
+        and not code.startswith("__attribute__", start)
+    )
+
+
+def _top_level_items(code: str) -> list[_Item]:
+    """Top-level declarations/definitions of `code` as offset spans."""
+    items: list[_Item] = []
+    depth = 0
+    start: int | None = None
+    brace: int | None = None
+    initialised = False
+    for i, ch in enumerate(code):
+        if start is None:
+            if ch.isspace():
+                continue
+            start, brace, initialised = i, None, False
+        if ch in "([{":
+            if ch == "{" and depth == 0 and brace is None:
+                brace = i
+            depth += 1
+        elif ch in ")]}":
+            depth = max(depth - 1, 0)
+            if depth or initialised:
+                continue
+            if ch == "}" and brace is not None and _is_function_head(code[start:brace]):
+                items.append(_Item(start, i + 1, brace, True))
+                start = None
+            elif ch == ")" and _starts_new_item(code, start, i + 1):
+                items.append(_Item(start, i + 1, None, False))
+                start = None
+        elif ch == "=" and depth == 0:
+            initialised = True
+        elif ch == ";" and depth == 0:
+            items.append(_Item(start, i + 1, brace, False))
+            start = None
+    return items
+
+
+def _enumerators(text: str) -> set[str]:
+    names: set[str] = set()
+    for match in re.finditer(r"\benum\b[^{;]*\{", text):
+        depth, i = 1, match.end()
+        part = ""
+        while i < len(text) and depth:
+            ch = text[i]
+            depth += ch in "([{"
+            depth -= ch in ")]}"
+            if (depth == 1 and ch == ",") or depth == 0:
+                found = _IDENT_RE.search(part)
+                if found:
+                    names.add(found.group())
+                part = ""
+            else:
+                part += ch
+            i += 1
+    return names
+
+
+def _declarator_names(tail: str) -> set[str]:
+    """The name each comma-separated declarator in `tail` declares."""
+    parts: list[str] = []
+    depth, part = 0, ""
+    for ch in tail:
+        depth += ch in "(["
+        depth -= ch in ")]"
+        if ch == "," and depth == 0:
+            parts.append(part)
+            part = ""
+        else:
+            part += ch
+    parts.append(part)
+    names: set[str] = set()
+    for declarator in parts:
+        pointer = _FN_PTR_NAME_RE.search(declarator)
+        if pointer:
+            names.add(pointer.group(1))
+            continue
+        flat = re.sub(r"\([^()]*\)|\[[^\]]*\]", " ", declarator)
+        idents = _IDENT_RE.findall(flat)
+        if idents:
+            names.add(idents[-1])
+    return names
+
+
+def _type_names(text: str) -> frozenset[str]:
+    names = set(_TAG_RE.findall(text)) | _enumerators(text)
+    if text.startswith("typedef"):
+        tail = text[text.rfind("}") + 1 :] if "}" in text else text[len("typedef") :]
+        names |= _declarator_names(tail.rstrip("; \t\n"))
+    return frozenset(names)
+
+
+def _definitions(source: str, code: str, items: list[_Item]) -> list[_Definition]:
+    """Type and macro definitions of the file, in source order."""
+    defs: list[_Definition] = []
+    for item in items:
+        text = code[item.start : item.end]
+        head = _IDENT_RE.match(text)
+        if item.is_function or head is None or head.group() not in _TYPE_HEADS:
+            continue
+        names = _type_names(text)
+        if names:
+            defs.append(
+                _Definition(
+                    item.start,
+                    item.end,
+                    names,
+                    frozenset(_IDENT_RE.findall(text)) - names,
+                    source[item.start : item.end],
+                )
+            )
+    no_comments = mask_comments(source)
+    for match in _DEFINE_RE.finditer(no_comments):
+        text = match.group().strip()
+        name = match.group(1)
+        defs.append(
+            _Definition(
+                match.start(),
+                match.end(),
+                frozenset({name}),
+                frozenset(_IDENT_RE.findall(text)) - {name, "define"},
+                text,
+            )
+        )
+    return sorted(defs, key=lambda d: d.start)
+
+
+def _used_definitions(defs: list[_Definition], seed: str) -> list[_Definition]:
+    used = set(_IDENT_RE.findall(seed))
+    selected: set[int] = set()
+    changed = True
+    while changed:
+        changed = False
+        for index, definition in enumerate(defs):
+            if index not in selected and definition.names & used:
+                selected.add(index)
+                used |= definition.uses
+                changed = True
+    return [defs[index] for index in sorted(selected)]
+
+
+def _comment_spans(source: str) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
+    return [
+        match.span()
+        for match in _COMMENT_OR_LITERAL_RE.finditer(source)
+        if match.group("comment") is not None
+    ]
+
+
+class _Scan:
+    """One lexical pass over a source file, shared by the recipes."""
+
+    def __init__(self, source: str) -> None:
+        self.source = source
+        self.code = _code_view(source)
+        self.items = _top_level_items(self.code)
+        self.comments = _comment_spans(source)
+
+    def function(self, symbol: str) -> tuple[_Item, int] | None:
+        """The definition of `symbol` and the offset of its body's ``{``."""
+        brace = find_definition_brace(self.source, symbol)
+        for item in self.items:
+            if brace is not None and item.is_function and item.brace == brace:
+                return item, brace
+        return None
+
+    def target(self, symbol: str) -> tuple[_Item, int]:
+        found = self.function(symbol)
+        if found is None:
+            raise RecipeError(f"no definition of {symbol!r} found")
+        return found
+
+    def doc_start(self, item_start: int) -> int:
+        """Offset where the comment block directly above `item_start` begins.
+
+        A comment is a doc comment only when no blank line separates it from the
+        item and nothing else shares its first line; a run of ``//`` lines is one
+        block. Anything else (a file header, a trailing comment on the previous
+        statement) is not.
+        """
+        start = item_start
+        for first, last in reversed([c for c in self.comments if c[1] <= item_start]):
+            gap = self.source[last:start]
+            line_start = self.source.rfind("\n", 0, first) + 1
+            if (
+                gap.strip()
+                or gap.count("\n") > 1
+                or self.source[line_start:first].strip()
+                or (
+                    start != item_start
+                    and not (
+                        self.source.startswith("//", first)
+                        and self.source.startswith("//", start)
+                    )
+                )
+            ):
+                break
+            start = first
+        return start
+
+    def definitions_used(self, seed: str) -> list[_Definition]:
+        """Type/macro definitions `seed` (code text) needs, transitively."""
+        defs = self._definitions()
+        used = set(_IDENT_RE.findall(seed))
+        selected: set[int] = set()
+        changed = True
+        while changed:
+            changed = False
+            for index, definition in enumerate(defs):
+                if index not in selected and definition.names & used:
+                    selected.add(index)
+                    used |= definition.uses
+                    changed = True
+        return [defs[index] for index in sorted(selected)]
+
+    def _definit

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"

tools.name: Skill

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. 	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## rea
REA provides reverse-engineering tools for local artifacts, native binaries, managed code, browser pages, and runtimes. Use the tool that directly answers the question; discover targets or inspect inventory only when needed. Tool results include inline Evidence and report their coverage and limitations.

1	"""Proposer input recipes: named, versioned, deterministic context builders.
     2	
     3	A *recipe* maps ``(unit id, source text, project root)`` to the text the proposer
     4	prompt renders in place of the whole unit file (RFC-0007, "Inputs: a context pack,
     5	not the whole file"). Recipes are the experiment's input factor, so each is pure
     6	and deterministic: the same arguments always yield the same context, and the
     7	recipe's ``ref`` (``name/vN``) is recorded on every property it helped propose
     8	(`Provenance.recipe`). A shipped version's behaviour is immutable; change a recipe
     9	by registering a new version.
    10	
    11	The v1 recipes are single-file (they read only the source text; the project root
    12	is part of the seam for the project-index recipes of RFC-0007 T1):
    13	
    14	- ``baseline``: today's whole file, minus any ``main`` and the leading file-header
    15	  comment (both leak the answer on ``examples/``).
    16	- ``sighted``: the target function with its doc comment, plus the type and macro
    17	  definitions it uses.
    18	- ``blind``: ``sighted`` without the target body: its signature, doc comment, and
    19	  only the definitions the *signature* uses, so nothing in the pack can be
    20	  transcribed from the implementation.
    21	
    22	The scan is lexical (comments, literals and directives masked), not a parse; it
    23	reads the same text ESBMC will, and degrades by omission rather than guessing.
    24	Only type and macro definitions are pulled in: objects the body reads (tables,
    25	globals), callees, and a struct reachable only through a variable declaration are
    26	out of scope for v1.
    27	"""
    28	
    29	from __future__ import annotations
    30	
    31	import re
    32	from collections.abc import Callable
    33	from dataclasses import dataclass
    34	from pathlib import Path
    35	
    36	from forseti.esbmc import find_definition_brace, mask_comments
    37	from forseti.esbmc.preprocessor import mask_string_literals
    38	from forseti.unit_id import unit_id_symbol
    39	
    40	
    41	class RecipeError(ValueError):
    42	    """A recipe could not build its context (unknown name, or no such function)."""
    43	
    44	
    45	@dataclass(frozen=True)
    46	class ProposalContext:
    47	    """The text a recipe built, and the recipe ``ref`` that built it."""
    48	
    49	    recipe: str
    50	    text: str
    51	
    52	
    53	@dataclass(frozen=True)
    54	class Recipe:
    55	    name: str
    56	    version: str
    57	    build: Callable[[str, str, Path], str]
    58	
    59	    @property
    60	    def ref(self) -> str:
    61	        """The provenance label, e.g. ``"blind/v1"``."""
    62	        return f"{self.name}/v{self.version}"
    63	
    64	
    65	_COMMENT_OR_LITERAL_RE = re.compile(
    66	    r'"(?:\\.|[^"\\\n])*"|\'(?:\\.|[^\'\\\n])*\'|(?P<comment>//(?:\\\n|[^\n])*|/\*.*?\*/)',
    67	    re.DOTALL,

   161	
   162	def _enumerators(text: str) -> set[str]:

     3	A *recipe* maps ``(unit id, source text, project root)`` to the text the proposer
     4	prompt renders in place of the whole unit file (RFC-0007, "Inputs: a context pack,
     5	not the whole file"). Recipes are the experiment's input factor, so each is pure
     6	and deterministic: the same arguments always yield the same context, and the
     7	recipe's ``ref`` (``name/vN``) is recorded on every property it helped propose

    12	is part of the seam for the project-index recipes of RFC-0007 T1):

Findings (all in the worktree, `src/` only; tests not reviewed):

1. `src/forseti/properties/recipes.py:216-248` and `:251-262` — dead duplicate code. Module-level `_definitions` and `_used_definitions` are copies of `_Scan._definitions` (`:339-370`) and `_Scan.definitions_used` (`:324-337`). The only callers are the `_Scan` methods, so the module-level ones are unreferenced. Cost: about 50 lines to delete. The simpler form is to keep one copy. Either delete the module-level pair, or, better, keep the module-level pure functions and drop the `_Scan` copies. The `_Scan` copy is the one the recipes use, so deleting the module-level pair is the smaller change.

2. `src/forseti/properties/recipes.py:57, 378-396, 435-445` — `project_root` is threaded through the whole stack and unused. All three builders do `del project_root`. It passes through `build_context`, `Recipe.build`, `prepare_proposal_request(project_root=...)` and `propose_source` (`store_root.parent`). The module docstring justifies it as "part of the seam" for future recipes. That is speculative generality. Cost: an extra parameter on 4 signatures, 3 `del` lines, and a `Path()` default that silently means the cwd. The simpler form is `build: Callable[[str, str], str]` and no `project_root` anywhere. Add it when a project-index recipe needs it.

3. `src/forseti/properties/recipes.py:53-62, 423-430` — `Recipe.name`, `version` and `ref` are derived, and `version` is always "1". The `ref` property, the `RECIPES` comprehension keyed by `recipe.name` and the three constructor calls exist to produce `"baseline/v1"` etc. A plain `RECIPES = {"baseline": _baseline, ...}` plus `f"{name}/v1"` would do the same. The immutability and versioning promise in the docstring is not enforced either. This one is minor and only worth doing if versions stay hypothetical.

4. `src/forseti/properties/recipes.py:46-50`, `proposer.py:79-87, 254, 263` — `ProposalContext` is a two-field wrapper that is unpacked at both use sites. `proposer.py` does `None if request.context is None else request.context.text` and `"" if request.context is None else request.context.recipe`. The `source_text` and `context` pair on `ProposalRequest` is also partly redundant. Simpler form: `ProposalRequest` carries `context: str | None` and `recipe: str = ""`. This removes the wrapper class, its export in `__init__.py`, and one of the None-checks.

5. `src/forseti/properties/recipes.py:99-106, 265-270, 65-68` — three separate comment and literal maskers. `_code_view` uses `mask_comments` plus `mask_string_literals`. `_comment_spans` has its own `_COMMENT_OR_LITERAL_RE`. `_definitions` calls `mask_comments(source)` again for `#define`. The `_comment_spans` regex re-implements lexing that `forseti.esbmc` already provides. Cost: a second lexer to keep in sync with the first. This is lower confidence, since the spans are needed for `doc_start`, and a shared helper might not exist. It is worth checking whether `esbmc` exposes comment spans.

6. `src/forseti/properties/recipes.py:282-294` — `_Scan.function` and `target` are two layers for one lookup. `function` loops over all items just to match `item.brace == brace`. The `brace is not None` check sits inside the loop, so it should come first (`if brace is None: return None`). `target` is a 3-line wrapper whose only job is to raise. Simpler form: one method that returns the item or None, with the raise in the two callers or a small `_require` helper.

7. `src/forseti/core/cli.py` (`_add_recipe_argument`, `scope` parameter) and the docstrings in `core/mcp_server.py` (`propose_tool`, `semantic_loop_tool`), `core/loop.py`, `core/propose.py` — the recipe description is written out three times: the CLI help, and two MCP docstrings that are near-verbatim copies. The loop and propose docstrings add more restatement. Simpler form: define the baseline/sighted/blind blurb once, for example as a constant next to `RECIPES`, and reuse it. Otherwise shorten the docstrings to one line pointing at `recipes.py`. Cost: three places to edit when a recipe changes. It also goes against the "comment sparingly" rule, for example `(#388)` tags and the `loop.py` recipe docstring.

8. `src/forseti/properties/recipes.py:1-27` — the module docstring is about 27 lines, including RFC references and a list of what v1 leaves out. The `doc_start`, `_starts_new_item` and `_ATTRIBUTE_RE` machinery does warrant explanation. The header and the "out of scope for v1" paragraph are more than the rule allows. Trim to a few lines.

9. `src/forseti/core/loop.py:188-189` — the `recipe is not None and mode != "propose"` check is a new `ValueError` branch for a caller error. It mirrors the `candidates` guard, so it is consistent, but it duplicates the CLI's "--mode propose only" scoping. This is optional and borderline. I would leave it.

Clean: the `store.py`, `model.py`, `discriminate.py`, `prompts.py` and `_proposal_request.py` changes are minimal and mirror the existing `provider`/`model` handling. The inline `recipe: str | None` plumbing through `loop`, `propose` and `mcp` is unavoidable.
